_about: Frameflow config for the video-critic skill (~/Talha_Khan/Claude/skills/video-critic): the critic desk of the 12-desk plan (P25.7.1), the table read (text) and the screening (stills) of The Daily Habit in one rubric. Rows and wording carried over from show.JUDGE_SYSTEM and show.SCREEN_SYSTEM on 6 Nov.
show: The Daily Habit, a fast daily news show for YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels (1080x1920): 8 stories in about 85 seconds, read aloud by the narrator Habit for Indians aged 18-30

rows.clarity: each story is understood in one listen, no jargon
rows.wit: the few witty lines land naturally; any forced or cringe joke scores 0 for this row; no joke is better than a forced one
rows.flow: handoffs make it one show, not a list
rows.accuracy: every claim is in the facts, nothing overstated, cautions respected
rows.variety: emotions and graphics fit and vary

rows.readability: graphic text and numbers readable at phone size, nothing cut off or overlapping
rows.framing: Habit and graphics placed well; nothing important in the bottom 420 px or the right 180 px below y 1000, where the platform buttons sit
rows.captions: readable, never covering a key graphic
rows.package: topic strip, countdown, bug and source chip clear and not cluttered
rows.habit: the narrator looks alive and his face fits the line

format_notes: the outro ends with "Make learning a Habit."
house_facts: the end card shows the pixel-art Habit (the studio's mascot look) while the show uses the drawn Habit
the bottom ~420 px of every frame are kept clear on purpose: YouTube Shorts and Reels lay their caption, buttons and progress bar over that strip; don't ask to fill it or move things into it
